title: Atomic Mass, Isotopes and Mass Defect
notes: **Atomic mass unit (u):** $1\,\text{u} = 1.6605 \times 10^{-27}\,\text{kg}$. Defined as 1/12 the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
**Isotopes:** atoms of the same element ($Z$) with different mass numbers ($A$). Same chemical properties, different nuclear properties.
**Mass defect:** $\Delta m = Zm_p + Nm_n - M_{nucleus}$. The nucleus weighs less than the sum of its parts because energy is released when the nucleus forms.
**Packing fraction:** $f = (M - A)/A$, where $M$ is the actual mass in u. It measures the deviation from the mass number and indicates nuclear binding stability.
**Binding energy per nucleon:** $BE/A$. It peaks around iron ($A \approx 56$) at about 8.8 MeV, explaining why both fusion of light nuclei and fission of heavy nuclei release energy.
